cards.title: Convex-roof entanglement of formation
cards.numerical_form: explicit optimal ensembles attain both the concurrence and entanglement convex roofs

checks.reason: The convex-roof definition and pure-state entropy are explicit.
Forward and inverse HJW maps reconstruct rho, and the constructive optimum attains E(C(rho)).

cards.title: Two-qubit spin flip and magic basis
cards.latex: tilde(rho)=(sigma_y tensor sigma_y) rho* (sigma_y tensor sigma_y)
cards.numerical_form: fixed 4x4 spin flip and a basis where it is coefficient conjugation

checks.reason: The state, density-matrix, and magic-basis maps are explicit.
Applying spin flip twice returns the original state or density matrix.
In the explicit magic basis, spin flip is coefficient-wise complex conjugation.

cards.title: Pure-state concurrence and entropy
cards.numerical_form: partial-trace entropy versus binary entropy of concurrence

checks.reason: Concurrence and mathcal E are printed explicitly.
Product states give zero and Bell states give one.
Random pure-state partial-trace entropies equal mathcal E(C).

cards.title: Mixed-state concurrence formula
cards.numerical_form: singular values of the proof tau matrix cross-checked against rho tilde(rho)

checks.reason: Both equivalent spectral definitions are explicit.
The tau singular values and rho-tilde product spectrum agree for the frozen campaign.
Pure states reduce to one nonzero lambda equal to pure-state concurrence.

cards.title: HJW decompositions, lower bound, and constructive optimum
cards.numerical_form: Takagi tilde-orthogonal states, signed preconcurrences, real rotations, and forward/inverse HJW maps

checks.reason: The HJW prescription, lower bound, and constructive optimum are explicit.
Generated and recovered HJW ensembles reconstruct rho to machine precision.
No sampled decomposition violates the analytic lower bound.
Takagi states and real rotations produce equal-preconcurrence ensembles attaining both C(rho) and E(C(rho)).

cards.title: Zero-concurrence decomposition
cards.latex: sum_j exp(2 i theta_j) lambda_j=0 when lambda1 <= lambda2+lambda3+lambda4
cards.numerical_form: lambda-polygon phase closure followed by the printed four-row Hadamard sign construction

checks.reason: The four-state phase construction and closure condition are explicit.
Independent mixtures of product states have zero concurrence and positive partial transpose.
Random and Bell-diagonal negative-branch states are reconstructed by four zero-concurrence subnormalized states.

cards.title: Pure-state asymptotic entanglement rate
cards.numerical_form: exact binomial-type mass and typical-subspace dimension rate through 32768 copies

checks.reason: The paper states the asymptotic conversion and communication-rate interpretation explicitly.
The exact binomial typical mass tends to one and its dimension rate tends to H2(p).

open_questions: The cited external converse and achievability proofs are not bundled; finite typical-subspace numerics do not replace those theorems.

cards.title: Previously proved rank-two scope
derived_from: the paper's historical statement about Ref. HW
cards.numerical_form: independent rank-one and rank-two optimal-decomposition campaign

checks.reason: The current paper explicitly states the earlier rank-at-most-two scope.
All frozen rank-one and rank-two cases attain the formula.

open_questions: The historical proof in Ref. HW is not included in the review bundle, so attribution and theorem-condition identity remain source-limited.

cards.title: Equal-entanglement optimal ensemble
cards.latex: E(psi_i)=mathcal E(C(rho)) for every nonzero component of an optimal ensemble
cards.numerical_form: per-component entanglement spread for every constructive optimal ensemble

checks.reason: The paper both attributes and independently proves an equal-entanglement construction.
The component spread is frozen, rather than inferred only from the ensemble average.

open_questions: The unpublished Uhlmann source cannot be audited, although the present paper's own construction is independently executable.

cards.title: Finite pure-state ensemble cardinality bound
derived_from: the real affine dimension d^2-1 of density matrices
cards.numerical_form: dimension count plus constructive ensembles using at most four states

checks.reason: The paper states the m<=16 prior-result bound.
A 4x4 density matrix has affine dimension 15, giving at most 16 pure-state points.

open_questions: The cited external source is not bundled; the dimension derivation verifies the bound but not its attribution.
